summary: Gerd J. R. Mevissen works in Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the Free University of Berlin, attested in 2017 and attested in 2026 as Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter.
Gerda Hartmann was an Indologist who earned her Ph.D. at Kiel University under Friedrich Otto Schrader (circa 1928–1932). She later worked at the Library of Congress from 1938 to 1940.

Gereon Kopf studied at Temple University (~1991–1996) and under postdoctoral mentor Yasuo Yuasa (~1996–1997). His career in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies includes research at J. F. Oberlin and Nanzan, plus teaching at Luther College and the University of Hong Kong.

Gergana Ruseva completed an MA in Indology at Sofia University (1995–2005). She served as a physicist at the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences (2000–2009) and held posts at Sofia University as a mathematics lecturer (2000) and Associate Professor (2012).

Gergely Hidas, an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, earned his master's at Eötvös Loránd University and his DPhil at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He served as a Khyentse Fellow at Eötvös Loránd University and a postdoctoral researcher at the British Museum.

Gergely Orosz is a scholar of Tibetology who completed a PhD at Budapest University of Technology and Economics (2018–2023), becoming an assistant professor there in 2023. He was also attested as a librarian at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences in 2002.

Gerhard Czerny was a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Vienna, the University of Rostock, and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg between 1923 and 1927, studying under Paul Althaus and Julius von Negelein.

Gerhard Meiser was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Albertus-Magnus-Gymnasium Regensburg, the University of Munich (~1972–1979), the University of Freiburg (~1979–1983), and the universities of Belgrade, Sarajevo, and Regensburg.

Gerhard Oberhammer earned his Ph.D. at Innsbruck under Erich Frauwallner and studied at the Sorbonne and under V. Raghavan. He held posts at Utrecht University (1961–1964) and the University of Vienna (1964–1997), working in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies.

Gerhard Wolf, an art and archaeology scholar, studied at Heidelberg University (~1972–1989). He held positions at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1992–1998), Trier University (~1998–2003), and the Max Planck Society (~2003).

Gerlach Royen was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University under Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck (~1918–1926). He taught at Gymnasium Immaculatae Conceptionis (1905–1911) and served as Professor of Comparative and General Linguistics at Utrecht University (1932–1943).
Gernot Böhme was a philosopher who studied at the University of Hamburg from around 1957 to 1965. He held a academic post at the Technical University of Darmstadt from approximately 1977 to 2002.
Gernot Rotter studied at the universities of Bonn, Tübingen, and under Annemarie Schimmel. He later held an academic post at the University of Hamburg from approximately 1984 to 2006.

Gernot Schmidt was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who completed his Ph.D. under Richard Karl Heinrich von Kienle at the Free University of Berlin and his habilitation at Bonn. He served as Professor of IE Linguistics at Bonn in 1980.

Gerrit Jan Held studied at Leiden University under J. P. B. de Josselin de Jong (Ph.D. 1935). He served as Professor of Cultural Anthropology at the University of Indonesia (1946–1950) and Visiting Professor at Yale University (1951–1952).

Gerrit Jan Meulenbeld was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda between ~1946 and 1954. He later served as associate professor of Indology at the University of Groningen from 1978 to 1986.

Gert Klingenschmitt studied under Karl Hoffmann at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, earning his PhD and Habilitation and serving as assistant. Specializing in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian studies, he held the Indogermanistik chair at the University of Regensburg (1983–2006).

Geshe Gendun Lodro was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Drepung Monastery under Khensur Ngawang Legden, he held faculty posts at Drepung Gomang Dratsang, the University of Hamburg (1967), and the University of Virginia (~1979).

Geshe Jampa Tegchok studied at Sera Monastery. A scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he served as abbot and resident teacher at Nalanda Monastery (~1982–1993) and as resident teacher at the Land of Medicine Buddha.
Geshe Karma Sonam is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts attested at Gyume Tantric College in 1987 and at Sera Monastery in 1992, and taught Elijah Sacvan Ary.
